ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal straight lines c and d, and they are marked as parallel with the same arrows. The oblique line b passes through both the upper straight line c and the lower straight line d. At the intersection of b and c, ∠3 is located above straight line c and on the left side of oblique line b; at the intersection of b and d, ∠13 is located below straight line d and on the right side of oblique line b. Reasoning: Given m∠3 = 43. Because c ∥ d, and b is a transversal, ∠3 and ∠13 are a pair of corresponding exterior angles in opposite interior-exterior positions, that is, alternate exterior angles. When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate exterior angles are equal, therefore m∠13 = m∠3 = 43.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $m\angle 3 = 43$. Find the measure of $\angle 13$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing the two horizontal lines c and d marked parallel, and the slanted line b crossing both of them. Angle 3 is at the upper intersection of b with c, outside the strip between c and d and on the left side of transversal b. Angle 13 is at the lower intersection of b with d, outside the strip and on the right side of transversal b. From the text, use m∠3 = 43. Since ∠3 and ∠13 are alternate exterior angles formed by transversal b cutting parallel lines c and d, they are congruent, so m∠13 = 43.
